title: Profile
subtitle: As an architect I translate strategic ambitions into target architectures and principles, and I design the operating model that makes them pay off. I'm principled about the horizon and pragmatic about the route. Information security, compliance and data governance are part of the design from day one, not a control added at the end. Among other things, I brought a qualified trust service for the Dutch notarial sector to certification at the highest eIDAS level, and architectural principles I developed were adopted by executive and senior management.

I've worked as an engineer, product owner and architect myself. That's why my designs are implementable, and why I speak the language of boardrooms and engineering teams alike. I like to stay close to the actual work: learning while building, validating in production, and handing over with clear documentation and clear ownership.

cards.title: Design the technology and the operating model that makes it pay off.
cards.text: Most architects stop at the diagram. I also design the policies, processes and teams that make it actually work.

cards.title: Architecture that leaves the whiteboard.
cards.text: Architectural choices only matter when teams can execute them. I design with that constraint in mind: few, strong principles, clear trade-offs, decisions that translate into standards and backlog items within weeks.

cards.title: Secure and compliant from day one.
cards.text: Information security, data governance and auditability are part of the design, not patched on later. Proven under eIDAS and ISO 27001, and now backed by CISSP.

cards.title: I translate between the people who need to agree.
cards.text: Board, risk, product and engineering only converge when someone makes the trade-offs explicit. I bring enough hands-on background to stay credible on each side, and I'm clear about where my role ends and theirs begins.
